A founder rejection or a failed replication now stops earning credit: settled competence (every reader of settlement.measured_outcomes), SOP proposal and ratification, and precedents withhold what the correction contains; the invalidating cognition.settled revision names the cause; a requalified cause returns the credit; nothing writes a grant, approval or capability state. Two further guards were needed and are included: a compilation that ended in a capability deficit is no longer a failed replication (false cause reproduced on pr196), and a refuted appraisal is left to the appraisal readers (listing it regressed an existing integration test). Reality tier: a cloud container, test keys, no founder device, VEPMC 0.

The same ablation is the gate's mutant "settlement ignores containment" (CAUGHT). A second simpler rule was tried and found wrong: skipping only the contained observation lets an earlier reading of the same claim earn the credit back (a mission that writes a note first reads each cognition claim twice and its closure cites only the later reading); the gate's mutant "an earlier reading of a withheld claim earns the credit back" covers it.
what_can_greg_do_now: After the founder signs a rejection of a delivered answer, or a later reading of the same signed question answers and fails, GREG stops counting that answer as evidence that its method is competent (compiler selection counts, capability disposition, conditional competence, learned routing, competency cells and the trust report all read the one corrected projection), stops learning a procedure from that mission, refuses to ratify a proposal that rests on it, and stops citing it as a precedent. It records which correction withheld the credit, keeps every earlier record, keeps the credit of readings nobody impugned (also inside the same mission), and returns the credit when the cause is requalified by evidence, without touching the registry, grants or approvals. Before this, the correction was recorded and nothing read it. Evidence: tests/unit/test_greg_evidence_corrections.py on a real Body in a cloud container with test keys; not founder-used.

A founder rejection is never requalified by evidence, so its credit stays withheld; a later founder critique that accepts the same closure does not lift it (corrections reads rejections only).
REPLICATION_FAILED is keyed by the signed sensor, not by the method: a later failing answer from another method withholds the first method's credit until a passing reading requalifies it.
Only the capability-deficit abstention was examined as a false replication. Other abstention states were not.

A claim is withheld whichever closure settled its earlier readings: in a mission that closed unmet and was later achieved, a verified failure of the same claim is withheld with a contained achievement reading. A closure-scoped fallback was tried and dropped because its result depended on whether an uncited re-observation happened in between.

A proposal already recorded with a mission that is later contained cannot be ratified and the same procedure id is not proposed again (sop.proposed is keyed by procedure). The same held before for a mission later refuted.

Credit is not withheld downstream of the reading: a mission that acted on a contained reading has its claim marked and is no procedure evidence, but its own sensor's settled outcome stays. A mission that consumes the output after the correction is recorded is still not held; that is the half of S43.A4 left open.

details:
WHAT WAS BUILT (canonical owners only; greg/missions.py and greg/authority.py untouched)
- greg/corrections.py: _containing (one helper), contained_receipts (rebuilt on it, same shape), contained_missions(journal) -> mission id -> {cause, cause_id, event}; APPRAISED = ("APPRAISAL_REFUTED",) excluded from containment; no_method_ran(output) and a per-reading "no_method" flag used only in the replication loop.
- greg/cognition/settlement.py: _measure(journal) -> (outcomes, withheld). It calls corrections.contained_receipts(journal) once; an observation whose receipt is listed settles nothing and its claim identity is dropped (scored as neither, as disputes are). measured_outcomes returns the first mapping. reconcile still calls measured_outcomes (an existing integration test patches that seam) and reads the cause only on a tick that invalidates something; the invalidating revision carries reason "withheld: correction <cause id> (<class>) ..." and withheld_by {cause_id, class, event}.
- greg/sop.py: closed_procedures subtracts corrections.contained_missions; its docstring is now a docstring (it sat after an import). ratify refuses a proposal that rests on a contained mission through the same line.
- greg/precedents.py: locally_appraised_missions excludes contained missions.
- scripts/ci/check_evidence_corrections_mutants.py: 9 mutants added (two older ones re-anchored): a refuted appraisal contains; a mission that acted on a contained reading is not named; a no-method compilation counts as a failed replication; a deficit read from data GREG did not produce; SOP learns from a contained mission; a contained mission is still a precedent; settlement ignores containment; the invalidating revision does not name its cause; an earlier reading earns the credit back. "A requalified cause stays contained" and "a source that moved on contains" already existed and now cover both projections through the shared helper. The gate is not new, so job 10 was not touched; only the stale comment above its step in job 8 was corrected.
- docs/mechanisms/MC-0003-correction-containment-credit.md: the nine requested fields, what corrections.py already had (justifications, claim labels, the early cutoff for claims, an unread OUT set), what was added, what was not transplanted (no stored network, no ATMS, no backtracking, no automatic re-run, no downstream credit withholding, nothing touching permission).
- acceptance/directive-sections.json: S43.A4 blocker reason only. It now reads "... what a measurement-impugning cause contains is withheld from settled competence, procedure proposals and precedents; a corrected claim does not yet hold a later mission that consumes its output". Class, coverage, unit, evidence and every count are unchanged.

WHERE THE RESULT DIFFERS FROM THE TASK TEXT, AND WHY
1. "skips any observation whose receipt is listed" is implemented as "withholds the claim". On a real Body a mission that writes a note first reads each cognition claim twice and the closure cites only the later receipt; skipping just that observation left the earlier reading crediting the method.
2. A refuted appraisal is not contained. Listing it kept credit withheld after the closure was verified again until the next propagation, and broke tests/integration/test_cognition_multi_claim_settlement.py::test_same_geometry_claims_settle_separately_and_corrections_replay. Settlement and SOP already read each closure's appraisal. The claim is still marked NEEDS_REVIEW.
3. Two guards beyond the list. Precedents were affected and did not read a corrected projection, so they got the filter. And on pr196, detaching the only fitting method and signing the same question again recorded REPLICATION_FAILED and asked the founder; with this change it would also have cost the first answer its credit, so a capability-deficit reading is no longer a replication (only GREG's own cognition receipts can say so).
